unsupported: The company traces its roots to 2004, when founder Sky began developing and racing suspension components in the Ultra4 4600 Class, earning first, second, and third-place finishes against four-link and V8-powered competitors.

Core processes include CNC machining of 6061-T6 aluminum rotor hats and other components, welding of weld-in bungs and brackets, and assembly of kits that combine Timken unit bearings, alloy hardware, and custom-fabricated brackets.
Customers are primarily off-road enthusiasts and racers building or upgrading vehicles for trail, desert, and competitive use.
The operation was born from a desire to prove parts on the race course before offering them to the public.
Sky states that every design is "continually tweaked to perfection through rigorous miles of trail and desert racing," a philosophy that ties product validation directly to competition results.
